subject: Sable Health onboarding: model shortlist & workload sizing
messages:
From: Alyssa Park <alyssa.park@sablehealth.com>
To: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Jorge Ramos <jorge.ramos@sablehealth.com>
Date: Tue, 24 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Sable Health — onboarding model shortlist & sizing

Hi Marissa,

Thanks again for the intro call yesterday. Attached is the workload export we discussed (Sable-Workload-CSV.csv) — it contains a 30-day sample of requests, a small prompt corpus, and a field that tags sensitive flows (PII). High-level context: most calls are short Q&A (avg prompt 120 tokens, avg response 280 tokens) but we have a subset of clinical-summary generation flows that require ~6,000 token context and produce larger outputs. Peak TPS observed in the sample is ~2.5 RPS.

Two asks for the handoff:
- Can you propose a model shortlist + recommended context window per flow?
- We also need a rough token-volume estimate and cost/latency implications for those flows so procurement has material for the SOW.

Looping in Jorge from procurement for any billing/procureIT questions.

Attachments: Sable-Workload-CSV.csv (csv)

Best,
Alyssa Park
Head of Product Operations | Sable Health
alyssa.park@sablehealth.com

From: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Alyssa Park <alyssa.park@sablehealth.com>
Cc: Jorge Ramos <jorge.ramos@sablehealth.com>; vivek_kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>; ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 24 Nov 2026 11:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Sable Health — onboarding model shortlist & sizing

Thanks Alyssa — got the sample and the notes. Sharing a concise handoff plan and initial recommendations so your team and procurement have what you need for the SOW. Attaching our onboarding checklist as a living doc.

Summary recommendations (shortlist & context buckets):
- Tier A (high-quality long-context): Redwood-Atlas-16k (16k context) — use for clinical-summary flows (~6k context), expected latency higher but best fidelity.
- Tier B (balanced cost/latency): Redwood-OPT-13B-q4 (8k context) — good for long-ish Q&A and multi-turn patient dialogues; lower cost with quantized weights.
- Tier C (throughput-oriented): Redwood-Mistral-7B-fast (4k context) — for lightweight Q&A and chat/bot flows.

Initial token-volume guidance (based on your sample):
- Baseline Q&A flows: 100k tokens/day (prompt + response)
- Clinical summary flows (10% of volume in sample): 300k tokens/day, with peaks up to 1.2M tokens/day during batch extraction windows
- Expected monthly: ~12M tokens (baseline) + burst capacity for summaries as needed

What we need from Sable to finalize sizing:
1) Confirm % of traffic that will be routed to each flow class (Q&A vs summaries).
2) Expected SLA for summary completion latency (e.g., 10s vs 30s).
3) Any regulatory constraints for key management or on-prem processing.
4) A sample of the longest single-context document you expect to send (if >6k tokens).

Next actions:
- Can we schedule a 30-min handoff call this week to confirm traffic split and SLA? I’m free Thu 11/26 10–12 PST or Fri 11/27 09–11 PST.

Attachments: Onboard-Checklist.pdf (pdf)

—
Marissa Cole
Senior Customer Success Manager | Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com

From: vivek_kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Alyssa Park <alyssa.park@sablehealth.com>; ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 25 Nov 2026 08:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Sable Health — onboarding model shortlist & sizing

Adding a few technical notes for the handoff — copying the shortlist Marissa proposed.

Operational/infra recommendations:
- For Redwood-Atlas-16k: plan for dedicated instances for summary jobs to avoid queuing; enable KV prefix cache for repeated patient-context tokens (saves ~20–30% token cost on multi-turn).
- Quantization: for Tier B/Balanced we recommend q4_0 for production to hit a good latency/cost point.
- Fallbacks: set routing policy so that when Atlas latency SLOs degrade, requests with non-clinical labels fall back to OPT-13B-q4. Keep summaries pinned to Atlas unless explicitly allowed.
- Expected GPU footprint (ballpark for sizing exercise):
  - Atlas-16k (p100/p4 equivalent): 1.6K tokens/sec per GPU for inferencing with batching tuned; plan 2–3 GPUs for steady-state summaries at sample load, 6 GPUs for peak batch windows.
  - OPT-13B-q4: ~3K tokens/sec per GPU.
  - Mistral-7B-fast: ~7–8K tokens/sec per GPU.

I'll populate a runtime worksheet and attach it (runtime-estimate-worksheet.xlsx) with the per-flow calculations so procurement can see the capacity vs cost tradeoffs.

—Vivek
Vivek Kulkarni
Lead Inference Engineer | Redwood Inference
vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com

2) For the dedicated instances you mention, what is the minimum contract term you recommend for predictable capacity?

Jorge: copying you for billing/contract questions.

Alyssa

Alyssa / Jorge — happy to take lead on the mutual action plan and procurement questions. Proposed MAP (mutual action plan):
- Week 0 (this week): finalize traffic split + SLA.
- Week 1: complete security review (we’ll use your SOC2 doc as baseline) + sign SOW (DocuSign link below).
- Week 2–3: provisioning + ingesting sample corpus into staging (redwood staging project).
- Week 4: smoke tests + latency/cost validation, then graduate to pilot.

Procurement answers:
- Per-token delta: we’ll run a short cost simulation once you confirm traffic split and provide an example 24-hour window (we can produce a 3-scenario delta: 0%/30%/100% to Atlas).
- Reserved capacity term: we recommend a 3-month minimum for predictable capacity, with monthly review for scaling.
